credential.label: Stripe test-mode secret or restricted key
credential.description: A test-mode secret (sk_test_…) or restricted (rk_test_…) key; prefer a restricted key with only the permissions this connector needs. It is sent only to api.stripe.com and files.stripe.com, stored encrypted, and never displayed.

guide.summary: Sandbox: test data only. One test-mode key over REST; resolve ids and account scope before acting.
guide.content:
# Stripe usage

Mode: sandbox. Connector purpose: Rehearsing billing changes

This is a SANDBOX Stripe connection. Nothing here is real money and none of these objects exist in production, so never answer a question about live revenue, payouts, or a named customer from this connector.

## Account and money

Confirm the account and environment before investigating a payment or moving
money. A Connect account's objects belong to that account, rather than the
platform's account. Sandbox objects do not establish anything about live
customers, revenue or payouts.

Resolve ids before acting. Stripe ids identify types: `cus_` customer, `sub_`
subscription, `ch_` charge, `pi_` PaymentIntent, `in_` invoice and `acct_`
account. A plausible-looking id can refer to a different object or to nobody.

Amounts are integers in the currency's minor unit: 1099 is 10.99 USD, while
10 is 10 JPY. Keep currencies separate when totaling balances or payments.

## Payment investigations

A PaymentIntent's `latest_charge` joins it to the charge holding the payment's
`outcome`, `failure_code` and `failure_message`. Follow that reference to
explain a decline. Search supports a documented field set for each resource;
charge search has no `payment_intent` field. Resolve the parent and follow its
reference when the needed relationship is not searchable.

Search is eventually consistent; use a direct object read to reconcile a
recent write. A POST's idempotency key identifies the exact operation and
parameters. Stripe v1 may prune keys after 24 hours, so reconcile the object
before attempting the operation outside that window. A new key can create a
second payment or refund.

## Data reduction and boundaries

Keep only the customer and payment facts the question needs. Reduce lists to
counts, totals or matching records before returning them to the conversation.
Use the account and balance summaries when their projections answer the task;
other account fields and balance transactions are available through the API.

Credential creation, customer/account sign-in links, secret payload expansions,
full Issuing card details, file uploads and the meter-event stream are outside
this connection's surface. Use the Dashboard or application server for those
flows. Single meter events remain available. A guest Checkout payment page is
available only when it is unbound to a Customer or Account and cannot manage
saved payment methods; use a payment link or hosted invoice for other cases.

## Conventions

- **Results:** `fields` narrows a read's result to the dot paths you name. `truncated` lists the dot paths a result cut for size; the ids that fetch what was cut stay in the result.
- **Hatch:** `stripe_api_search` finds this API's operations and reads no account data, `stripe_api_details` shows one operation's contract, and `stripe_api_read` calls a reviewed read. `stripe_api_write` calls a reviewed write, and every call to it needs approval. An operation without a reviewed verdict is refused; these are refused by design: `POST /v1/account_links`, `POST /v1/account_sessions`, `POST /v1/accounts/{account}/login_links`, `POST /v1/billing_portal/sessions`, `POST /v1/customer_sessions`, `POST /v1/ephemeral_keys`, `POST /v1/file_links`, `POST /v1/files`, `POST /v1/financial_connections/sessions`, `POST /v1/link_account_sessions`, `POST /v1/terminal/connection_tokens`, `POST /v1/terminal/onboarding_links`, `POST /v2/billing/meter_event_session`, `POST /v2/billing/meter_event_stream`, `POST /v2/core/account_links`.
- **Writes:** a write is sent once and never retried. When its outcome is unknown, read the target before repeating it. A write that takes `idempotencyKey` may be repeated with the same key and arguments while the vendor retains it.
- **Errors:** codes come from the vendor's statuses and error facts, never its prose. `not_found` means the record does not exist; this API tells absence from a permission gap. `conflict` means: HTTP 409 when the request conflicts with another request, including a concurrent use of the same idempotency key; HTTP 429 with code lock_timeout when another request holds the object's lock.
- **Withheld values:** a value withheld for safety reads `"[redacted]"`. Writes refuse whole marker values and withheld links; longer prose may mention the marker. Paths and queries refuse any containment.

tools.name: get_stripe_account_info
tools.description: Read the Stripe account this key reaches: id, name, country, default currency, mode, and connected account. Use it to confirm scope first.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result, e.g. ["accountId"]. It only narrows the result.

connectedAccount.description: Set when every call acts as this account.

tools.name: get_balance_summary
tools.description: Read the account's available and pending Stripe balance per currency, in minor units. Excludes balance transactions; list those with stripe_api_read.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result, e.g. ["livemode"]. It only narrows the result.

available.description: Funds available to pay out, per currency.

pending.description: Funds not yet available, per currency.

tools.name: stripe_api_search
tools.description: Find Stripe API operations by keyword or path. Returns up to 8 compact matches with the tool that calls each; reads no account data.

query.description: Keywords or a path, e.g. refund charge.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous search with the same query.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

matched.description: The request or response field this operation was found by; call its tool to read the field.

truncated.description: Entry labels cut for size; stripe_api_details on that method and path returns them whole.

tools.name: stripe_api_details
tools.description: Read one Stripe API operation's request contract: path, query and body parameters with types and required names. Reads no account data.

path.description: The path template from search, or a concrete path.

param.description: Return only this parameter, in full.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous details call with the same method, path and param.

body.description: Body content type and schema. When paged: this page's properties, the required names it delivers or chunks, and the schema's other keywords on the page that carries them.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

of.description: The piece this text belongs to, such as parameters.limit.

text.description: Part of that piece's JSON; join the parts in page order, then parse them.

truncated.description: Labels cut for size; their full text arrives as chunks.

page.description: Present when the contract exceeds one answer: pass nextCursor back for the next pieces.

tools.name: stripe_api_read
tools.description: Call a reviewed Stripe API read, including reviewed read-only POST. The operation index checks arguments before anything is sent. Pass page.nextCursor as cursor; starting_after or ending_before record-id anchors are allowed only on the first request, without cursor. v1 parameters use bracketed form encoding; v2 bodies are JSON. Quote PDFs use the confined files origin.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /v1/customers/cus_123. No query string.

method.description: GET by default; another method only for an operation search routes here.

body.description: Body for a reviewed read-only POST.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from this same read; omit raw query anchors when continuing.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.

param.description: Vendor parameter restored from cursor; pass nextCursor as the top-level cursor.

tools.name: stripe_api_write
tools.description: Call a reviewed Stripe API write; method and path are stated for approval, and the operation index checks arguments first. POST sends an Idempotency-Key; DELETE sends none. v1 bodies are form-encoded, including nested fields; v2 bodies are JSON. Upload files in the Stripe Dashboard.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /v1/customers/cus_123. No query string.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

body.description: Request body as JSON fields, named as details lists them; form operations are encoded for you.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

idempotencyKey.description: Reuse this key with the exact original arguments; a key is generated and returned when omitted for a supported method.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.
